noveltyJustification: Eight findings are new (plugin packaging, seam inventory, bridge gaps, matcher mismatch, repo hook inventory, per-extension verdicts, bundle sizing, cwd semantics); one reframes the Hermes bundle precedent.
answeredQuestions: Which lifecycle seams exist for plugins and hooks, and which Pi extensions must be ported, deferred or dropped?
ruledOut: Porting all eighteen Pi extensions to native plugins

label: A harness plugin is a Cordis object with optional inject and an apply(ctx) field registered as a profile row by package name; a repo-local plugin must be installed into the profile as a bundle (file:/link:), and without HMR a new or changed plugin reports restart-required.

The lifecycle seams are tools/pre-execute, tools/execute, tools/post-execute, tools/result, agent/pre-step, agent/turn-stopping, agent/created, agent/disposed, session/event, turn/start, turn/end, approval/request, fs/write-intent, fs/edit-intent, fs/delete-intent, compaction/* and commands/change.

The shipped Claude Code hook bridge maps SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SubagentStart and SubagentStop; it does not support PreCompact or SessionEnd, leaving the compact context injector and session-end cleanup without a bridge point.

Claude literal matchers are exact and case-sensitive, while harness tool names are lowercase, so the repo's existing Bash, Write|Edit, WebFetch, Task and AskUserQuestion matchers select nothing and a rewritten .dsh/hooks.json is required.

The repo already carries the hook implementations: .claude/settings.json wires 9 PreToolUse, 5 PostToolUse, 3 UserPromptSubmit, 8 SessionStart, 3 Stop, 1 SessionEnd and 1 PreCompact entries over runtime-neutral Node scripts.

Sixteen of the nineteen Pi extensions are bridge-served by a rewritten hook config; task-dispatch-guard needs adaptation for the subagent tool name and payload, and goal-context plus session-compact-context need a native plugin.

A single repo bundle is the smaller move only for the residual guards: the shipped bridge carries the bulk, so repo-guards would hold two plugins and optionally a task-dispatch adapter, one install and one SYNC entry.
Hooks run in the session directory with CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR set per run, and a relative configPath resolves from the launching directory, so the dispatch builder must pin the cwd to the repo root.
Headless disables HMR, so plugin changes cannot hot-reload in a dispatch; a lineage installs or updates the repo bundle before its run, never mid-run.

direction: Porting all eighteen Pi extensions to native plugins
reason: The scripts already exist and most hook points are served by the shipped Claude Code bridge.
Its capitalized tool matchers never match the harness's lowercase tool names.
Plugin resolution is profile-package based, so a repo bundle must be installed into the profile first.
